opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alyssa Rose (employee ID E026) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E026.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alyssa Rose (E026) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; role (Analyst) does not own Payroll, so admin is not applicable. Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alyssa Rose (E026) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors with basic training max out at read for any system; requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Alyssa Rose (E026) requested write access to Payroll. The Security DB indicates she is a contractor with basic security training, which limits her maximum access to read for any system (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Since the requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, the granted level is the maximum: read. (The HR note claiming full-time employment conflicts with the Security DB record, which is authoritative here.)

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Alyssa Rose (E026) requests write access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- HR note: full_time Analyst, recommend write
- Security note: contractor with basic security training, recommend read

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so admin not applicable. Write would be allowed.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training. Security DB typically has authoritative info. The Security note says "Security DB shows... contractor with basic security training".

So per the security note, Alyssa is a contractor with basic training → max read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

I'll go with read. Let me submit the decision.
